correctness.rationale: Weighted matrix-tree determinant exactly equals the unnormalized Walsh sum. Odd-order parity proves every coefficient odd; Cayley--Pruefer signing with vertex-sign sum 1 attains magnitude 1. In even order the reduced Laplacian is all-odd and n-2 integer row differences prove divisibility by 2^(n-2). Balanced factorizable signs give zeros. Reversing the signs of a tree on n-1 vertices changes the reduced Laplacian from -yy^T to M-yy^T, and adj(M)=product(weights)11^T; with sum(y)=-1 gives exact absolute determinant 2^(n-2). Both directions and spectral normalization checked. Independent Prüfer/FWHT, signed determinant and witness tests replayed from the standalone package code; exhaustive only n<=6, universal argument is algebraic.

value.rationale: The complete-graph tree-incidence indicator is a canonical determinantal Boolean signal. Its smallest positive Walsh multiplier is the exact inverse stability constant of an associated full-dimensional convolution operator, and the theorem settles that invariant for every n. Nontrivial even-order 2-adic sharpness via a tree-flip determinant construction and infinitely many zero frequencies make the result an exact natural infinite-family structural finding rather than a routine parity test. It distinguishes singular even orders from invertible odd orders with exact spectral stability.
